phys_1_5 G1.issue: The anchoring stool demo could not work as written: a load wholly over the legs does not tip a stool with a nudge. The jerrycan must overhang the seat edge beyond the leg. A stool tips only when the vertical line through the combined centre of gravity of stool plus load falls outside the tipping edge. A 20 kg jerrycan standing wholly over the legs cannot do that with a gentle nudge, so the original demonstration would simply not topple. The phenomenon is kept (the teachers' choice), but the set-up now says the jerrycan overhangs the seat edge, which makes the toppling real and the explanation correct. Checked by comparing moments about the tipping leg: jerrycan 200 N × 0.10 m = 20 N·m against the narrow stool's own weight 50 N × 0.15 m = 7.5 N·m (topples), and 80 N × 0.30 m = 24 N·m for a wider, heavier stool (rocks back). TEACHER DECISION: please try the demonstration with your own stool and adjust the overhang (about 10 cm beyond the leg is a good start) until the narrow stool topples and the wide one rocks back. CLAUDE'S PROPOSAL on one corner of the seat so that part of it overhangs the seat edge beyond the leg (its weight then acts outside the triangle formed by the legs) and gently nudges it, the stool topples dramatically. Strikingly, a wider, lower, heavier four-legged stool with the same jerrycan placed at the same corner with the same small overhang barely tilts

The Kiswahili words are common everyday terms, but they have not been checked against the Kiswahili physics textbook used in your schools. TEACHER DECISION: please confirm or correct the Kiswahili words and supply the standard term for 'moment' and 'centre of gravity'. CLAUDE'S PROPOSAL 1. Write 'MOMENT = TURNING EFFECT' in large letters on the board BEFORE defining it formally. Add a small word bank beside it for English learners with Kiswahili beside each word: force (nguvu), weight (uzito), pivot (egemeo), balance (usawa), topple (kupinduka); ask learners which Kiswahili word their textbook uses for 'moment' and add it. Learners may explain an idea first in Kiswahili or with a labelled sketch before writing it in English.

phys_1_5 G12.issue: Corrected three Kenyan engineering examples in Lesson 5 (Citi Hoppa 'battery packs', 'Eldoret cereal board', Turkana pot carriers) and put them on a poster to save time. Citi Hoppa mainly runs single-deck buses and diesel buses have no 'battery packs'; an upper deck is not narrower; 'Eldoret cereal board' is not an institution (the National Cereals and Produce Board, NCPB, has depots in Eldoret); a 'wide-brimmed pot base' is not how head-ring carrying works. TEACHER DECISION: please confirm the examples you want (for instance the bus operator and the silo location) and whether the pot-carrying example is appropriate for your learners. CLAUDE'S PROPOSAL Three Kenya-relevant engineering examples are shown on a mini-poster that students read while they build their models (no teacher talk time): (1) Double-decker buses seen in Nairobi — heavy engine, gearbox and fuel tank kept low in the chassis, wide wheel track; (2) Grain storage silos such as those of the National Cereals and Produce Board (NCPB) in Eldoret — wide circular base, low centre of mass; (3) Water pots carried on the head using a cloth ring — the ring holds the rounded pot so that its centre of gravity stays directly above the carrier.
